examples.en: My son grumbles about his food every day these days.

examples.ko: 밥투정하지 말고 반찬도 골고루 먹어 보세요.
examples.en: Don't complain about the food; try eating all the side dishes too.
My little brother fusses over his meals, so Mom is very worried.

examples.ko: 저녁마다 밥투정하면 나중에 배고프다고 해도 안 줄 거예요.
examples.en: If you grumble about dinner every night, I won't give you food later even if you say you're hungry.
I also often fussed over my food when I was little.
How should I handle a child who grumbles about food?

explain: '편식하다'는 좋아하는 음식만 골라 먹는 것이고, 밥투정은 먹기 싫다고 떼를 쓰거나 불평하는 행동에 초점이 있어요. 주로 아이에게 쓰고, '밥투정을 하다'처럼 말해도 같아요.
explain_en: '편식하다' means eating only the foods you like, while 밥투정 focuses on whining or complaining about not wanting to eat. It is mostly used for children, and you can also say '밥투정을 하다'.

examples.ko: 아이 입가에 밥풀이 하나 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There is a grain of rice stuck at the corner of the child's mouth.

examples.ko: 손에 붙은 밥풀을 떼어 내기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to get the rice stuck on my hand off.
I sealed the envelope with a few grains of rice.

examples.ko: 설거지할 때 그릇에 말라붙은 밥풀은 물에 불려요.
examples.en: When I wash dishes, I soak the dried-on rice grains in water.

examples.ko: 옷에 밥풀 묻은 줄도 모르고 하루 종일 다녔어요.
examples.en: I went around all day without noticing there was rice on my clothes.

examples.ko: 김밥을 싸다 보니 손이 밥풀투성이가 됐어요.
examples.en: While rolling gimbap, my hands ended up covered in rice.

explain: '밥알'과 거의 비슷하지만, 입가나 손, 옷에 붙어 있는 밥 한 톨을 말할 때 특히 잘 써요. '입가에 밥풀이 묻었어요'처럼 '붙다·묻다'와 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It is close to '밥알', but it is especially natural for rice stuck to the mouth, hands or clothes. It often goes with verbs like '붙다' and '묻다', as in '입가에 밥풀이 묻었어요'.

examples.en: I stayed in my room the whole weekend.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 청소했더니 방구석에 먼지가 많이 쌓여 있었어요.
examples.en: I cleaned for the first time in a while, and dust had piled up in the corner of the room.
One sock turned up in the corner of the room.
The child got scolded and went into a corner of the room to cry.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 방구석만 지키고 있기 답답해요.
examples.en: It's stifling to stay cooped up in my room all day.
The remote must be somewhere in a corner of the room.

explain: 방 안의 구석이라는 뜻도 있지만, 집이나 방에만 틀어박혀 있는 모습을 투덜거리듯 말할 때도 많이 써요. 말투가 편해서 글보다 대화에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It can mean a corner inside a room, but it is also used in a grumbling tone for staying shut up at home or in your room. The tone is casual, so it fits conversation better than formal writing.

examples.en: My uncle farts a lot, so his nieces and nephews tease him.
My little brother is a farter who even does it in his sleep.
Whoever the farter is, the smell is terrible!
The kids laughed and called their friend a fart machine.

examples.ko: 방귀쟁이 강아지 때문에 거실 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: Because of our gassy puppy, I opened the living room window.

examples.ko: 우리 반 방귀쟁이는 수업 중에도 참지 못해요.
examples.en: The class farter can't hold it in even during lessons.

explain: 방귀를 자주 뀌는 사람이나 동물을 장난스럽게 부르는 말이에요. '겁쟁이', '욕심쟁이'처럼 '-쟁이'가 붙은 말이라 아이들 말이나 가족 사이 농담에 어울리고, 어른에게 직접 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요.
explain_en: This is a playful name for a person or animal that passes gas often. Like '겁쟁이' and '욕심쟁이', it uses the '-쟁이' ending, so it suits kids' talk and family jokes, and it can be rude if said directly to an adult.

examples.ko: 장례식장 입구에서 조의금을 내고 방명록에 이름을 썼어요.
examples.en: At the funeral hall entrance, I gave my condolence money and wrote my name in the guest book.
There is a guestbook at the café entrance.

examples.ko: 여행 간 곳마다 방명록에 한마디씩 남겼어요.
examples.en: At every place I visited on my trip, I left a few words in the guestbook.

examples.ko: 박물관 방명록을 읽다 보니 외국인 방문객이 많았어요.
examples.en: Reading the museum guestbook, I saw there were many foreign visitors.
In the past, every personal website had a guestbook.
Where do I sign the guestbook?

explain: 결혼식, 장례식, 전시장 같은 곳에서 이름과 짧은 글을 남기는 책을 말해요. '방명록을 쓰다·남기다'라고 하고, 예전 인터넷 홈페이지의 방명록 게시판에도 썼어요.
explain_en: It is the book where you leave your name and a short note at weddings, funerals and exhibitions. You say '방명록을 쓰다' or '방명록을 남기다', and the word was also used for the guestbook boards on old websites.

examples.ko: 일본 대표 방문단이 오늘 서울에 도착했어요.
examples.en: The Japanese delegation arrived in Seoul today.

examples.ko: 학생 방문단을 위해 안내 책자를 준비했어요.
examples.en: We prepared a guide booklet for the visiting student group.

examples.ko: 시청에서는 해외 방문단과 함께 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: At city hall, we had lunch together with the overseas visiting group.
The visiting group has as many as thirty people.

examples.ko: 방문단에 통역사가 두 명 포함되어 있어요.
examples.en: The visiting group includes two interpreters.

examples.ko: 방문단은 이틀 동안 공장을 둘러볼 거예요.
examples.en: The delegation will tour the factory for two days.

explain: 여럿이 한 팀으로 어딘가를 찾아갈 때 쓰고, '해외 방문단', '학생 방문단'처럼 앞에 누가 가는지 붙여요. 뉴스나 행사 안내에서 자주 보이고, 한두 사람이 오면 '방문객'이나 '손님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when many people visit a place as one team, with a word before it saying who, as in '해외 방문단' or '학생 방문단'. You see it in news and event notices, while one or two people are called '방문객' or '손님'.

examples.en: I hit my toe on the door threshold and it really hurts.

examples.ko: 아기가 방문턱을 넘어 거실로 기어 나왔어요.
examples.en: The baby crawled over the threshold into the living room.
The threshold was high and I almost tripped on it.
I put anti-slip tape on the door threshold.
The robot vacuum can't get in because of the threshold.

examples.ko: 방문턱은 밟으면 안 된다고 할머니께서 말씀하세요.
examples.en: Grandmother says you shouldn't step on the door threshold.

explain: 방문 아래쪽에 가로로 대 놓은 턱을 말해요. 그냥 '문턱'이라고도 하는데, 방문턱은 방 문에 있는 것에 한정해서 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the raised ledge across the bottom of a room door. People also just say '문턱', and 방문턱 fits when you mean specifically the one on a room door.

examples.ko: 이 빵에는 방부제가 들어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: This bread has no preservatives in it.
I want to eat food without preservatives.
Without preservatives, a lunch box spoils quickly.

examples.ko: 방부제를 많이 쓰면 건강에 안 좋다고 해요.
examples.en: They say using a lot of preservatives is bad for your health.
Check the ingredients that are used as preservatives.
A little preservative goes into cosmetics too.

explain: 음식이 상하지 않게 넣는 물질로, 화장품에도 쓰여요. 일상에서는 '방부제'라고 하고, 식품 성분표에서는 '보존료'라는 말도 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a substance added to keep food from spoiling, and it is used in cosmetics too. In daily talk people say '방부제', and on food ingredient labels you may also see the term '보존료'.

examples.ko: 요즘 방송가에서는 새 예능 이야기가 많아요.
examples.en: These days there is a lot of talk about new variety shows in the broadcasting world.
A strange rumor is going around the broadcasting world.

examples.ko: 이 배우는 방송가에서 인기가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: This actor is very popular in broadcasting circles.
Personnel changes in the broadcasting industry were in the news.

examples.ko: 방송가는 가을이 되면 새 프로그램으로 바빠져요.
examples.en: The broadcasting world gets busy with new programs in autumn.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 방송가를 떠나 해외에서 활동해요.
examples.en: That singer left the broadcasting scene and works overseas.

explain: '연예가', '출판가'처럼 '-가'가 붙어 방송과 관련된 사람들이 모인 세계를 가리켜요. 소문이나 분위기를 말할 때 잘 어울리고, 직업이나 업계 구조를 말할 때는 '방송계'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Like '연예가' and '출판가', the '-가' ending points to the world of people involved in broadcasting. It suits talk about rumors or the mood of that scene, while '방송계' is also used when talking about the profession or industry structure.

examples.en: He worked in the broadcasting industry for twenty years.
Senior people in broadcasting helped me a lot.
The broadcasting industry changes fast, so it's tough.
How should I prepare to get into the broadcasting industry?

examples.ko: 방송계의 오래된 관행이 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: Long-standing practices in the broadcasting industry are becoming a problem.

examples.ko: 그녀는 방송계를 떠나 작은 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: She left the broadcasting field and opened a small shop.

explain: 방송 분야 전체를 직업과 업계의 세계로 볼 때 쓰는 말이에요. '방송가'와 거의 같게 쓰지만, 일하는 분야나 진로를 말할 때는 방송계가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It treats broadcasting as a whole as a professional and industry world. It is used almost like '방송가', but 방송계 sounds more natural when you talk about a field of work or a career path.

examples.ko: 그는 질문을 받자 방어적 태도를 보였어요.
examples.en: When he was asked the question, he became defensive.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 후반에 방어적으로 경기하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our team decided to play defensively in the second half.
If you talk from a defensive stance, the conversation gets hard.

examples.ko: 주식 시장이 불안해서 방어적 투자를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The stock market is unstable, so I'm investing defensively.
Why are you reacting so defensively?

examples.ko: 회의에서 방어적 발언만 하는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone who makes only defensive remarks in meetings.

explain: 뒤에 '태도, 자세, 반응'처럼 명사가 오고, '방어적인 태도'나 '방어적으로 말하다'처럼 활용해서도 써요. 반대말은 '공격적'이고, 사람에게 쓰면 비판받을까 봐 움츠리거나 변명하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It comes before a noun such as '태도', '자세' or '반응', and it is also used in forms like '방어적인 태도' and '방어적으로 말하다'. Its opposite is '공격적', and for a person it suggests shrinking back or making excuses for fear of criticism.

examples.en: Beads of sweat formed on my forehead.
Dew has formed in drops on the blades of grass.
Water is dripping drop by drop from the faucet.
Rainwater fell in drops from the edge of the eaves.
Tears rolled down the child's face drop by drop.

examples.ko: 컵 바깥에 물이 방울방울 맺혀 있어요.
examples.en: Water has formed in droplets on the outside of the cup.

explain: 작은 물방울이 하나하나 맺히거나 이어서 떨어지는 모습에 써요. 땀, 눈물, 이슬, 빗물과 잘 어울려요. 땀이 맺힌 모습만 말할 때는 '송골송골'도 써요.
explain_en: It describes small drops forming or falling one after another, and it goes well with sweat, tears, dew and rainwater. For sweat beading up, '송골송골' is also used.

examples.ko: 고속도로 옆에 방음벽이 높게 서 있어요.
examples.en: A tall soundproof wall stands beside the highway.

examples.ko: 방음벽을 세운 뒤로 소음이 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Since the soundproof wall was built, the noise has dropped a lot.
Thanks to the sound barrier, the house has become quiet.

examples.ko: 방음벽에 새 모양 스티커를 붙인 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some places put bird-shaped stickers on the sound barrier.

examples.ko: 방음벽 높이를 더 올려 달라고 주민들이 요청했어요.
examples.en: Residents asked for the sound barrier to be made taller.

examples.ko: 철도 옆 방음벽 때문에 창밖 풍경이 안 보여요.
examples.en: Because of the sound barrier next to the railway, I can't see the view outside the window.

explain: 주로 도로나 철도 옆에 세운 큰 벽을 말할 때 써요. 집 안의 소리 문제는 '방음이 잘 되다', '층간소음'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to the large walls built beside roads and railways. For noise problems inside a home, people say things like '방음이 잘 되다' or '층간소음'.

examples.en: The government announced new fire prevention measures.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 재발 방지책이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: This incident definitely needs measures to prevent a recurrence.

examples.ko: 정보 유출 방지책은 직원 교육부터 시작해요.
examples.en: Measures to prevent data leaks start with staff training.

examples.ko: 방지책 없이 같은 실수가 반복되고 있어요.
examples.en: The same mistake keeps repeating without any preventive measure.

examples.ko: 미끄럼 사고 방지책으로 바닥에 매트를 깔았어요.
examples.en: As a way to prevent slipping accidents, we laid mats on the floor.

examples.ko: 더 나은 방지책에 대해 회의에서 이야기했어요.
examples.en: We talked about better preventive measures in the meeting.

explain: '재발 방지책', '사고 방지책'처럼 막아야 할 일을 앞에 붙여 써요. '대책'은 문제가 생긴 뒤의 대응까지 넓게 가리키고, 방지책은 어떤 일을 막기 위한 구체적인 방법에 쓰여요.
explain_en: It takes the thing to be stopped before it, as in '재발 방지책' and '사고 방지책'. '대책' is broader and can include responses after a problem occurs, while 방지책 is a concrete way to stop something from happening.

examples.ko: 여름이 오기 전에 창문에 방충망을 달았어요.
examples.en: Before summer came, I put a screen on the window.

examples.ko: 창문을 열어 두면 벌레가 들어오니까 방충망을 꼭 닫아 주세요.
examples.en: Bugs come in if the window is open, so please be sure to close the screen.
The screen is torn, so mosquitoes come in.
Cleaning the screen is easy with a damp cloth.
The screen got a hole, so I replaced it.
I only feel at ease once I close the balcony screen too.

explain: 창문과 문에 붙박이로 달아 두는 망이에요. '모기장'은 침대나 텐트 위에 치는 천이라 달라요. 보통 '방충망을 달다·닫다·바꾸다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the mesh fixed on windows and doors. A '모기장' is different: it is a net hung over a bed or tent. People usually say '방충망을 달다', '닫다' or '바꾸다'.

examples.ko: 겨울 산에 갈 때는 방한복을 꼭 입으세요.
examples.en: Be sure to wear cold-weather gear when you go to the mountains in winter.
The winter gear is thick, so it's hard to move around.
I was surprised that the winter gear cost more than I expected.

examples.ko: 방한복 안에 얇은 옷을 여러 겹 입었어요.
examples.en: I wore several thin layers under my winter gear.
I bought winter gear for the child as well.
This winter gear stays warm even at minus twenty degrees.

explain: 그냥 '겨울옷'이라고 하면 일반적인 두꺼운 옷이고, 방한복은 등산, 야외 활동, 현장 작업처럼 추위를 막는 기능이 중요한 옷에 어울려요. '방한복을 입다·챙기다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '겨울옷' is ordinary winter clothing, while 방한복 suits clothing whose cold-blocking function matters, such as for hiking, outdoor activities or work sites. You say '방한복을 입다' or '챙기다'.

examples.en: When you study, your smartphone is the troublemaker.

examples.ko: 저는 늘 방해꾼이 된 것 같아서 미안해요.
examples.en: I'm sorry, I feel like I'm always in the way.

examples.ko: 방해꾼처럼 굴지 말고 조용히 있어 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't act like a pest and stay quiet.
There is no one getting in the way between us.

examples.ko: 영화 속 방해꾼 역할을 맡은 배우가 인기예요.
examples.en: The actor who plays the meddler in the movie is popular.
I don't know what to do about the person who keeps disrupting us.

explain: '장사꾼', '일꾼'처럼 '-꾼'이 붙은 말이고, 일을 방해하는 사람에게 써요. 스마트폰처럼 방해가 되는 물건을 비유로 부를 때도 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '훼방꾼'이 있어요.
explain_en: Like '장사꾼' and '일꾼', it uses the '-꾼' ending and is used for a person who gets in the way of something. It can also be used figuratively for things like a smartphone that disrupts you. A similar word is '훼방꾼'.

examples.en: Please clear the obstacles from the road.
There are no big obstacles to this plan.

examples.ko: 방해물 없이 달릴 수 있는 길이에요.
examples.en: It's a road where you can run without anything in the way.
You can solve the obstacles one at a time.

examples.ko: 시야를 가리는 방해물 때문에 앞이 안 보여요.
examples.en: I can't see ahead because something is blocking my view.
Be careful not to bump into anything in the way.

explain: 사람을 가리키는 '방해꾼'과 달리 물건이나 상황처럼 일을 막는 것에 써요. '장애물'과 비슷한데, 달리기나 길 위에서 몸으로 넘어야 하는 것에는 '장애물'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Unlike '방해꾼', which refers to a person, 방해물 refers to things or situations that block a task. It is close to '장애물', but for things you physically get over, such as in a race or on a path, '장애물' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I hung an air freshener in the car.

examples.ko: 방향제 냄새가 너무 강해서 머리가 아파요.
examples.en: The air freshener smell is so strong that I get a headache.

examples.ko: 현관에 놓은 방향제가 벌써 다 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The air freshener I put in the entryway has already run out.
I chose a lemon scent for the bathroom air freshener.
I air out the room by opening a window instead of using an air freshener.
The scent in this air freshener lasts a long time.

explain: 차 안, 현관, 화장실처럼 공간에 좋은 향을 내는 물건이에요. 몸에 뿌리는 '향수'와 다르고, 나쁜 냄새를 없애는 데 초점이 있는 '탈취제'와도 달라요.
explain_en: It is a product that gives a pleasant scent to a space such as a car, entryway or bathroom. It differs from '향수', which you put on your body, and from '탈취제', which focuses on removing bad smells.

examples.en: My grandfather farms dry fields.
In this area there is more field farming than rice-paddy farming.
Field farming is hard when there is little rain.
Chili peppers and beans are mostly grown in dry fields.
I went to buy plastic sheeting for farming the field.
We were short of hands for the field work, so the neighbors helped.

explain: 물을 대는 논에서 벼를 키우는 '논농사'와 짝이 되는 말이에요. 밭에서는 채소, 콩, 고추 같은 것을 키워요. '농사를 짓다'는 ㅅ 불규칙이라 '밭농사를 지어요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '논농사', growing rice in flooded paddies. In 밭, people grow things like vegetables, beans and chili peppers. '농사를 짓다' is a ㅅ-irregular verb, so you say '밭농사를 지어요'.

examples.en: Mom goes out to work in the field early in the morning.
Let's have lunch together when the field work is done.
Field work in summer is really hard because of the heat.
Grandmother hurt her back while working in the field.

examples.ko: 밭일 때문에 손에 흙이 늘 묻어 있어요.
examples.en: Because of the field work, there is always soil on my hands.
Gloves and a hat are a must for field work.

explain: 밭에서 하는 일을 가리켜요. '농사'가 농업 전체라면, 밭일은 풀 뽑기나 수확처럼 밭에서 몸을 움직여 하는 일에 가까워요. '밭일을 하다·나가다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means work done in a field. While '농사' covers farming as a whole, 밭일 is closer to hands-on tasks in the field such as weeding or harvesting. You say '밭일을 하다' or '밭일을 나가다'.

examples.ko: 엄마는 오전 내내 뜨거운 햇볕 아래서 밭일해요.
examples.en: Mom works in the field all morning under the hot sun.
Grandmother gets up every dawn and works in the field.

examples.ko: 어제 하루 종일 밭일해서 온몸이 쑤셔요.
examples.en: I worked in the field all day yesterday, so my whole body aches.
I listen to the radio while working in the field.
If you're going to work in the field, you need a wide-brimmed hat.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 밭일하지 않고 집에서 쉬어요.
examples.en: When it rains, I don't work in the field and rest at home.

explain: '밭일을 하다'와 뜻이 같아요. '농사짓다'는 농사 전체를 말하고, 밭일하다는 밭에서 몸을 움직여 일하는 모습에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It means the same as '밭일을 하다'. While '농사짓다' covers farming as a whole, 밭일하다 focuses on physically working in the field.

examples.ko: 삶은 국수를 찬물에 헹궈서 체에 밭쳐요.
examples.en: I rinse the boiled noodles in cold water and drain them in a sieve.
I strained the broth to make it clear.

examples.ko: 두부를 면 보자기에 밭치면 물기가 빠져요.
examples.en: If you strain tofu through a cotton cloth, the water drains out.

examples.ko: 튀김 기름을 식힌 뒤 거름망에 밭치세요.
examples.en: After the frying oil cools, strain it through a filter.
I add a little salt to the strained stock.
I'm straining the fruit juice finely.

explain: 체나 거름망에 액체를 부어 건더기를 걸러 낼 때 써요. 소리가 [받치다]로 같은 '받치다'(아래에서 떠받치다)와 헷갈리기 쉬워요. '체에 밭치다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when you pour liquid through a sieve or strainer to separate out solids. It sounds the same, [받치다], as '받치다' (to prop up from below), so it is easy to mix up. A common phrase is '체에 밭치다'.

examples.ko: 배불리 먹고 나서 허리띠를 한 칸 풀었어요.
examples.en: After eating my fill, I loosened my belt by one notch.
Today I ate my fill of meat.

examples.ko: 아이들이 배불리 먹을 수 있게 밥을 많이 했어요.
examples.en: I made lots of rice so the children could eat until they were full.

examples.ko: 명절에는 온 가족이 배불리 먹고 이야기를 나눠요.
examples.en: At the holidays the whole family eats well and chats.

examples.ko: 배불리 먹지 못한 날이 많았다고 할머니가 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother said there were many days when she couldn't eat enough.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나면 친구들과 배불리 먹으러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: After the exams, I'm going out to eat until I'm full with my friends.

explain: 그냥 '많이'보다 배가 가득 찰 만큼 충분히라는 느낌이에요. 거의 '먹다', '먹이다'와 함께 쓰고, 반대로 배고픈 상황에서는 '배불리 먹지 못하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '많이', it gives the feel of enough to fill your stomach. It is almost always used with '먹다' or '먹이다', and for the opposite you say '배불리 먹지 못하다'.

examples.ko: 샤워기 배수구가 막혀서 물이 안 내려가요.
examples.en: The shower drain is clogged, so the water won't go down.
There is a lot of hair stuck in the drain.
A smell came up from the drain, so I cleaned it.
I bought a product to unclog the sink drain.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 길가 배수구로 물이 넘쳤어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so water overflowed from the drain by the road.

examples.ko: 배수구 덮개는 자주 씻어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You need to wash the drain cover often.

explain: 욕실이나 싱크대, 길가에서 물이 빠져나가는 구멍이에요. '하수구'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 하수구는 더러운 물이 흘러가는 길이나 관까지 넓게 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is the opening where water drains away in a bathroom, sink or roadside. '하수구' is used similarly, but it can also refer more broadly to the channel or pipe that carries dirty water.

examples.en: Of all the swimming strokes, the backstroke is the easiest for me.

examples.ko: 배영은 얼굴이 물 밖에 있어서 숨쉬기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In the backstroke your face is out of the water, so it's easy to breathe.
I swam fifty meters using the backstroke.
I'm practicing the backstroke kick.

examples.ko: 배영을 배우고 나서 수영이 더 재미있어졌어요.
examples.en: After learning the backstroke, swimming became more fun.

examples.ko: 배영할 때는 천장을 보면서 팔을 돌려요.
examples.en: When doing the backstroke, you look at the ceiling and rotate your arms.

explain: 자유형, 평영, 접영과 함께 수영 종목 이름이에요. 누워서 천장이나 하늘을 보며 헤엄치는 영법이라 숨쉬기는 편하지만 방향을 보기 어려워요. '배영을 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a swimming stroke name, alongside 자유형, 평영 and 접영. You swim on your back looking at the ceiling or sky, so breathing is easy but it is harder to see where you are going. You say '배영을 하다'.

examples.en: School is a place of learning where you learn together with friends.
A library becomes a place of learning open to everyone.

examples.ko: 이 센터는 어르신들의 배움터로 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This center is popular as a place of learning for seniors.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 배움터에서 한글 수업을 들어요.
examples.en: I take Korean alphabet classes at the learning center in my neighborhood.
I made new friends while attending the learning place.

examples.ko: 마을 배움터는 누구나 무료로 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: The village learning center is free for anyone to use.

explain: '배우다'와 '터'가 합쳐진 말로, 학교나 교육 시설을 부드럽게 부르는 표현이에요. 일상에서 '학교', '학원'은 흔히 쓰고, 배움터는 표어, 간판, 글에서 잘 보여요.
explain_en: It combines '배우다' and '터' and is a soft way to refer to a school or educational facility. In daily speech people say '학교' or '학원', while 배움터 shows up in slogans, signs and writing.

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 못 먹는 아이도 백김치랑 밥은 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Even a child who can't eat spicy food eats white kimchi with rice well.

examples.ko: 백김치는 고춧가루를 쓰지 않아서 맵지 않아요.
examples.en: White kimchi doesn't use chili powder, so it isn't spicy.
White kimchi goes well with these noodles.
Before the holiday, Mom made white kimchi.
The white kimchi broth is refreshing, so I keep drinking it.
Pear and chestnut go into white kimchi.

explain: 빨간 배추김치와 달리 고춧가루 없이 담근 하얀 김치예요. 맵지 않아서 아이나 매운 음식을 못 먹는 사람에게 권하기 좋아요. 보통 '백김치를 담그다·먹다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike red napa cabbage kimchi, this is white kimchi made without chili powder. It isn't spicy, so it is good to offer to children or people who can't eat spicy food. You say '백김치를 담그다' or '먹다'.

examples.en: In summer I played ball with friends on the sandy beach.
A wide sandy beach stretches on endlessly.
Walking barefoot on the sandy beach feels good.
The children are building a sandcastle on the beach.
The sand is hot during the day, so wear slippers.

examples.ko: 해 질 무렵 백사장 위로 노을이 번졌어요.
examples.en: Around sunset, the glow spread over the beach.

explain: 하얀 모래가 넓게 펼쳐진 바닷가나 강가를 말해요. '해수욕장'은 사람들이 놀러 가는 장소 전체이고, 백사장은 그 안의 모래밭 자체를 가리켜요. 비슷한 말로 '모래사장'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a wide stretch of white sand by the sea or a river. '해수욕장' is the whole place people go for a beach outing, while 백사장 is the sandy area itself. A similar word is '모래사장'.

examples.en: I made baekseolgi for the baby's first birthday.
Baekseolgi is a white, soft rice cake.
I bought a pack of baekseolgi at the rice cake shop.
This baekseolgi has raisins in it.
The baekseolgi is still warm, so it's delicious.
I gave the guest a piece of baekseolgi as well.

explain: 쌀가루를 시루에 쪄 낸 하얀 떡이에요. 아기의 백일이나 돌 같은 축하 자리나 이사, 고사 때 나누어 먹는 전통이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a white rice cake made by steaming rice flour. It is traditionally shared at celebrations such as a baby's 100th day or first birthday, and at housewarmings and ritual offerings.

examples.en: The family gathered for the baby's 100th-day celebration.

examples.ko: 백일잔치 때 떡을 이웃에게 나눠 줘요.
examples.en: At a 100th-day celebration, people share rice cakes with their neighbors.
Last year we held my nephew's 100th-day party at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 백일잔치는 아기가 태어난 지 백 일쯤 됐을 때 해요.
examples.en: A 100th-day celebration is held when the baby is about a hundred days old.
I got an invitation to a 100th-day party from my friend.
After the 100th-day party ended, they sent me photos.

explain: 아기가 태어난 지 백 일쯤 됐을 때 건강하게 자란 것을 축하하는 잔치예요. 첫 생일의 '돌잔치'와 짝으로 말하고, 백설기 같은 떡을 나누는 풍습이 있어요.
explain_en: It is a party celebrating a baby's healthy growth at about a hundred days old. It is spoken of alongside the first-birthday '돌잔치', and a custom of sharing rice cakes such as 백설기 goes with it.

examples.en: An eel is a long, slippery fish.
I ate grilled eel as a summer health food.
A big eel is swimming in the aquarium.

examples.ko: 뱀장어 요리를 파는 식당이 근처에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a restaurant nearby that sells eel dishes.
I saw a live eel at the market.
I caught a fish that looks similar to an eel.

explain: 식당에서는 보통 '장어'로 줄여 불러요. 장어라고 부르는 물고기에는 다른 종류도 있어요. '장어구이', '장어덮밥'처럼 요리 이름에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: At restaurants it is usually shortened to '장어'. Other kinds of fish are also called 장어. It often appears in dish names such as '장어구이' and '장어덮밥'.

examples.en: After doing sit-ups, the skin on my belly feels tight.

examples.ko: 뱃가죽을 잡고 살을 얼마나 뺄지 고민했어요.
examples.en: I pinched my belly and wondered how much weight to lose.
A surgery scar remains on my belly.
A frog's belly skin is thin and soft.
Even when I diet, only my belly doesn't slim down.
The area near my belly itched, so I scratched it.

explain: 배를 덮은 살갗을 가리켜요. 배에 붙은 지방은 '뱃살'이라고 해서 구별하고, 뱃가죽은 다소 직설적이고 편한 말투예요.
explain_en: It refers to the skin covering the belly. The fat on the belly is called '뱃살', which keeps the two apart, and 뱃가죽 is a somewhat blunt, casual word.

examples.en: As soon as I got on the boat, I got terribly seasick.
I took seasickness medicine and boarded the boat.
Seasickness gets worse the higher the waves are.

examples.ko: 저는 뱃멀미 때문에 제주도 갈 때 비행기를 타요.
examples.en: Because of seasickness, I take a plane when I go to Jeju.
To reduce seasickness, look into the distance.
I suffered from seasickness and couldn't even eat lunch.

explain: 배를 탔을 때 생기는 멀미예요. 그냥 '멀미'라고도 하지만, 배에서 생긴 것임을 분명히 할 때 뱃멀미라고 해요. 차에서는 '차멀미'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the motion sickness you get on a boat. You can also just say '멀미', but 뱃멀미 makes it clear it happened on a boat. For cars, the word is '차멀미'.
